findings.finding: The stated CI parity contract is broader than the evidence and proposed guard. Two workflows (`codeql.yml` and `pr-review.yml`) do not install Python, while AC5 says the runner pin must match “what every workflow’s `uv python install` names.” A guard that only compares existing `uv python install` occurrences can pass when a workflow that runs Python/uv has no explicit interpreter setup at all.
findings.suggestion: Define the authoritative CI scope precisely: identify every workflow/job that executes the F0-equivalent test units or invokes `uv run` for Python tests. Require each such job to explicitly install/use 3.11, or intentionally exclude non-test workflows in the parity test with a documented reason. Make the guard fail for an in-scope Python test workflow that lacks an explicit 3.11 declaration, rather than treating absence as agreement.

findings.finding: The warm-up does not establish that all 18 units can resolve and execute under 3.11. The 14 plugins are separate uv projects with separate environments; a root-cwd warm-up can only warm the root environment. A plugin can still fail on its first 3.11 resolution because of a lockfile, marker, or transitive dependency issue even though its project metadata says `>=3.11`.
findings.suggestion: Before landing, validate a clean worktree with no relevant `.venv` directories and run the complete discovered F0 suite under the new commands. In particular, confirm all plugin units provision successfully on 3.11 and that concurrent first-run provisioning does not produce cache/venv contention failures. Update the risk wording so it does not imply the single warm-up prebuilds all plugin environments.

findings.finding: Pinning changes the local failure mode for contributors whose environment prohibits uv downloads or has no usable 3.11 interpreter. Previously, such machines could run F0 on an ambient 3.12/3.13; after this change they will fail before tests run. That is the intended correctness trade-off, but the failure may be reported as an F0 infrastructure error and be confusing in offline or enterprise-managed environments.
findings.suggestion: Document the prerequisite and remediation in the F0/operator documentation: install or make available Python 3.11 (for example, `uv python install 3.11`) before running F0. Ensure the existing failure output preserves uv’s actionable interpreter-install error rather than replacing it with a generic runner failure.

findings.finding: The proposed “one owner” protection can become tautological if the argv test and parity test both merely consume `suite_units.UV_RUN`. In that form, refactoring the constant could preserve the tests while producing an invalid command prefix or removing the explicit argument from the constructed command path.
findings.suggestion: Keep `UV_RUN` as the implementation owner, but make the tests independently inspect behavior: assert the final `build_command()` token sequence contains `uv`, `run`, `--python`, `3.11` in valid uv option position; independently assert the constant/workflow/version-file value is `3.11`. For version files, assert the exact expected root-plus-14-plugin path set, not only that all currently tracked files agree.  Overall, argv pinning plus scoped `.python-version` files is the correct solution and appropriately preserves reproducible retry commands. The plan needs a tighter definition and enforcement of the CI authority, plus clean-worktree validation across all separate plugin projects before it is ready. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

The CI interpreter-presence and version checks search raw workflow text, including comments. A workflow can run an unpinned active `uv run` while containing `# uv python install 3.11`; that comment satisfies both `"uv python install" in ...` and the version regex, so both guards pass even though CI has reverted to ambient interpreter selection. This undermines AC5’s requirement that removing CI’s effective pin fails the guard.
findings.suggestion: Inspect executable `run:` script content rather than arbitrary YAML text, at minimum excluding shell/YAML comments before matching. Add a regression fixture or mutation test with a commented-out install and active `uv run` to prove it fails.

findings.finding: The claimed “no uv invocation escapes” guard only rejects the exact double-quoted source fragments `"uv"` and `"uvx"`. A new unpinned call written idiomatically as `subprocess.run(['uv', 'run', ...])` (or assembled through a variable) bypasses the check entirely, while all three newly added per-site pin tests remain green. Thus the stated protection against the exact recurrence mode—a fourth unpinned call site—is not actually enforced.
findings.suggestion: Use an AST-based assertion targeting subprocess command construction/calls, or otherwise inspect both quote styles and command-list construction robustly. Add a negative test/source fixture demonstrating that a single-quoted bare `uv run` is rejected.  Overall assessment: The runtime pinning and version files implement the primary behavior correctly, but the anti-rot tests required by AC5 are bypassable in concrete, ordinary edits. Ship with fixes to make the guards enforce their advertised invariant. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
